conventions.convention: The countable canonical index set is nonempty, finite or explicitly enumerated countably infinite; energies are finite real numbers and weights are strictly positive. Nonnegative sums are suprema over finite subsums. Canonical probabilities exist only where 0 < Z < infinity. Logarithms are natural, and H_g is entropy relative to the specified weights.

The diagonal coefficient inner product is linear in its first variable. The operator domain is exactly the square-summable families whose energy-weighted coefficients are square summable; it is part of the operator data. Empty finite index sets are allowed.

Measures need not be complete. Almost-everywhere assertions hold outside a measurable null set. The nonnegative integral is the supremum of simple-minorant integrals; 0 times infinity is zero, while infinity minus infinity is undefined.

On a noncomplete measure space, dominated convergence integrates the canonical measurable limit representative; an arbitrary specified almost-everywhere representative is integrated only if it is measurable.

Lattice models use dimension d ≥ 1, a nonempty finite alphabet, a finite possibly empty list of bounded translated interactions of finite range, cubic boxes, and free boundary energies. Other boundaries require an explicit uniform surface-order energy comparison.

Finite Shannon and conditional entropies sum only over positive probabilities; conditional laws are formed only for positive marginal probability. Mutual-information equality means factorization at every pair, including pairs outside the joint support.

The general Gibbs theorem assumes full AC, a nonzero complex Hilbert space, a semibounded self-adjoint operator, positive inverse parameter, and trace-class Gibbs operator at the fixed parameter. Parameter differentiation additionally requires the stated local summable second-moment envelope.
The finite-shell microcanonical law is uniform on states with energy in the half-open interval [0, Delta), provided that shell is nonempty.

load_bearing.statement: For measurable f ≥ 0, the integral is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions s ≤ f; real integrability means finite integral of |f|. Completeness of the measure is not assumed.

For the countable canonical model, suppose every compact interval K contained in J admits a summable nonnegative envelope a_i with g_i(1+|E_i|²)exp(-beta E_i) ≤ a_i for all i and beta in K. Then Z is positive, finite and C² on J; its first two derivatives are the corresponding energy-moment sums, -∂beta log Z is the mean, ∂beta² log Z is the variance, and H_g = log Z + beta times the mean with absolute convergence.

For measurable complex f_n converging almost everywhere to f and dominated almost everywhere by a nonnegative integrable measurable g, the canonical finite pointwise-limit representative f_0, set to zero where no finite limit exists, is measurable and integrable; integrals converge to its integral and the L¹ distance tends to zero. The same conclusions hold for f when f is measurable.

Under AC, let A be self-adjoint on a nonzero complex Hilbert space with regular spectral PVM supported in [a, infinity), and suppose its bounded Gibbs operator K_beta is trace class for beta > 0. Then K_beta is injective and admits a finite or countable complete orthonormal energy eigenbasis, with positive finite partition trace and normalized positive trace-one density. Bounded-observable expectations have the absolutely convergent eigenbasis formula. On an open positive parameter set with the stated local summable second-moment envelope, the Gibbs operators remain trace class and the canonical derivative and entropy identities hold.

For measurable nonnegative f_n increasing pointwise to f on a measure space, their integrals increase to the integral of f, including infinite values. The nonnegative integral is additive and positively homogeneous, and the real integrable integral is linear.

For every fixed beta > 0, the free-cube normalized log-partition sequence of the bounded finite-range lattice model has a finite limit. An energy on the same configurations differing uniformly by at most C_b L^(d-1), with C_b independent of L, has the same normalized log-partition limit.
For a finite joint probability law, the positive-support Shannon and conditional entropy definitions satisfy H(M,R) = H(R) + H(M|R) and H(M|R) ≥ 0.

For a finite or explicitly enumerated countable index set, the diagonal coefficient inner-product space is complete; its energy-weighted domain is a dense linear subspace containing finite-support vectors, and coordinate multiplication defines a linear map into the coefficient space. The empty finite index set is included.

concerns.concern: Step 3.1 says that each threshold counted in s_n is counted at the even-index threshold in s_(n+1), 'so s_n ≤ s_(n+1)'. Each new threshold has half the old coefficient, so that observation alone gives only half the required bound. The immediate completion is to count both new thresholds 2k-1 and 2k for each old threshold k. The asserted monotonicity and theorem remain correct.

The Proof's Given paragraph says 'degeneracy g ≥ 1', whereas the Statement uses m for the ground-state cardinality and g_i for arbitrary positive weights. The proof itself correctly uses W_0 and the weighted ground-state distribution; the introductory g is undefined and should be m.

seams_checked.note: This is a page-order prerequisite. The assigned items do not invoke a nonsmooth-equilibrium item as a logical supplier or strengthen its convex-analysis conclusions.

The dephasing theorem's Statement and A1 retain AC, the nonzero complex Hilbert space, semibounded self-adjoint operator and trace-class Gibbs hypothesis. Its finite-multiplicity discrete energy basis follows from injectivity of the exponential and finite multiplicities of nonzero compact Gibbs eigenvalues. The consumer retains complete degenerate energy blocks and asserts Cesàro convergence.

The integral bridge identifies the same simple minorants, simple integrals and extended supremum convention. The cutoff proof uses that definition directly. The continuum pressure proof invokes the explicit bridge before applying shared Tonelli suppliers; it does not claim that the finite-alphabet lattice pressure theorem establishes a continuum limit.
